    Week 3: Control flow and functions

    Last updated on 2026-11-03 | Edit this page

    Overview

    Questions

    • What will I learn in Week 3?
    • How should I spend my time this week?

    Objectives

    • Plan your Week 3 study time using the time plan.
    • Find the videos, sections, Concepts Bridge and practice task for the week.

    This week your programs start to make decisions, repeat steps and reuse code. These ideas are the heart of programming.

    Learning goals

    By the end of this week you can:

    • make a program choose between actions with if, elif and else;
    • repeat steps with while and for loops, and stop or skip with break and continue;
    • write your own functions that take values and return a result;
    • plan a solution in pseudocode, write a simple sorting method yourself, and trace it in the PyCharm debugger.

    Time plan (6 hours)

    Block Time What you do
    Watch 1 h 22 m 8 short videos
    Read & practise 2 h 8 m Sections 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3, with Level 1 exercises
    Concepts Bridge 0.5 h Problem solving and sorting
    Build 2 h Grade calculator
    Total 6 h

    Read & practise includes an optional 1 h online drop-in or Q&A session. Do the Watch block first, then read, then bridge, then build. You can mix videos and reading by day: for example, watch T#19 and then read Section 3.1.

    Watch (1 h 22 m)

    All links open in the Telusko Python for Beginners (Full Course) playlist.

    # Video Length Look for
    T#19 If Elif Else Statement 15:38 How Python picks one branch, and why the indentation matters
    T#20 While Loop 12:43 The condition is checked before every repeat
    T#21 For Loop 7:27 Looping over a list and over range()
    T#22 Break Continue Pass 10:20 What each keyword does to a loop
    T#32 Functions in Python 11:13 How to define a function with def and call it
    T#33 Function Arguments 7:52 Passing values in, and getting a value back with return
    T#34 Types of Arguments 9:55 Positional, keyword and default arguments
    T#70 Bubble Sort 7:21 How neighbouring values are compared and swapped. You will trace this in the Bridge.

    Read & practise (2 h 8 m)

    Read each lesson, type and run every example in PyCharm, then do the Level 1 exercises. Create one .py file per section, such as section_3_1.py. Where a lesson says to use VS Code, use PyCharm instead: File > New > Python File, then click the green arrow to run.

    Lesson Read Level 1 exercises
    Conditionals All sections. Short Hand and Nested Conditions can be a quick skim. 1 to 3
    Loops While Loop, Break and Continue, For Loop, The Range Function, Nested For Loop. Skim For Else and Pass. 1 to 8
    Functions Everything down to “Function with Default Parameters”. Skim the arbitrary-arguments and dictionary-unpacking sections. 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 13

    Notes:

    • Section 3.3 exercise 3 asks you to check types. Skip that part; just add up the numbers.
    • Section 3.2 Level 2 and 3 use files from the data folder (countries.py, countries-data.py). In this course they are in assets/data. They are optional extras.
    • Section 6.1 (modules) is taught in Week 6.

    Concepts Bridge (0.5 h)

    Bridge: solving problems and sorting. Learn the understand, pseudocode, code, test process. Then write bubble sort yourself from pseudocode, trace it in the PyCharm debugger, and compare it with Python’s sorted().

    Build (2 h)

    Practice task: grade calculator. Enter marks, store them, and report the average and a grade, using functions and if/elif. Write short pseudocode first. This task is for practice and is not marked.

    Optional

    Only if you have time. Nothing here is needed to finish the week.

    Videos (Telusko)

    • T#22.1 Break vs continue vs pass
    • T#23 Printing patterns
    • T#24 For-else
    • T#25 Prime numbers
    • T#35 **kwargs
    • T#36 Global vs local
    • T#37 Pass list to function
    • T#38 Fibonacci
    • T#39 Factorial
    • T#68 Linear search
    • T#69 Binary search
    • T#71 Selection sort

    Find these in the playlist.

    Lessons

    • Section 6.1: Modules (taught in Week 6)

    Reading

    • Driscoll, M. (2017) Python 101, Chapters 4 to 6 and 10. Available at: https://web.archive.org/web/20260309033724/https://python101.pythonlibrary.org/

    Next week

    Week 4 covers recursion, functional programming and error handling. You will rewrite a similar grade calculator in a functional style. Week 4’s task is self-contained, so you do not need your Week 3 files.

    Key Points
    • Each week has four blocks: Watch, Read & practise, Concepts Bridge and Build.
    • The whole week fits in 6 hours or less.
